Task: Write a quick note explaining why TCP differs from UDP.

TCP differs from UDP primarily in reliability and connection orientation. TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) establishes a connection before data transfer, guarantees delivery through acknowledgments and retransmissions, ensures ordered packet delivery, and manages flow and congestion control. This makes it ideal for applications requiring accuracy, like web browsing or file transfers. UDP (User Datagram Protocol), by contrast, is connectionless and sends packets (datagrams) without handshakes, acknowledgments, or guaranteed delivery. It offers lower latency and overhead, making it preferable for real-time applications like video streaming, online gaming, or DNS queries where speed matters more than perfect reliability.
